question: For women under thirty-five years old, how long of trying to conceive without success is generally used to define infertility?
explanation: Standard medical guidelines use twelve months of regular unprotected intercourse as the baseline time frame before evaluating a younger woman for infertility. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T21#GNS312_U1_T21_h1)

question: Why do doctors start fertility evaluations much sooner for women aged thirty-five and older?

options.A: Due to increased frequency of male factor infertility in older couples
options.B: Because older women have higher rates of cervical mucus abnormalities
options.C: To account for the faster age-related drop in egg supply
options.D: To prevent patients from developing chronic pelvic inflammatory disease

explanation: A woman's egg supply and quality decline more rapidly after age thirty-five, making early testing and treatment necessary. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T21#GNS312_U1_T21_h1)

question: Which hormonal imbalance is a key feature of polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)?
explanation: Having high levels of male hormones (androgens) disrupts normal egg development and is a major sign used to diagnose PCOS. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T21#GNS312_U1_T21_h2)

question: A patient with extreme weight loss and intense athletic training stops having her period. What is the main cause?

options.A: Autoimmune destruction of the primordial ovarian follicles
options.B: Direct mechanical blockage of the fallopian tubes by adipose tissue
options.C: Hypersecretion of prolactin from the posterior pituitary gland
options.D: Suppression of gonadotropin-releasing hormone from the hypothalamus

explanation: Physical stress and low body energy tell the brain to slow down reproductive hormone signals, which stops ovulation. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T21#GNS312_U1_T21_h2)

question: What is the most common infection that leads to blocked fallopian tubes and tubal infertility?
explanation: Infections like chlamydia and gonorrhea can travel upward and cause pelvic inflammatory disease, which leaves scar tissue in the fallopian tubes. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T21#GNS312_U1_T21_h3)

question: A patient has severe menstrual cramps, ongoing pelvic pain, and blocked fallopian tubes seen on an X-ray test. Which condition is the most likely cause?
explanation: Endometriosis happens when tissue similar to the lining of the uterus grows outside of it, causing painful inflammation and scarring that can block the tubes. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T21#GNS312_U1_T21_h3)

question: Which specific type of uterine fibroid grows directly into the main cavity of the uterus and interferes with pregnancy attachment?
explanation: Submucosal fibroids sit right beneath the inner uterine lining and distort the space where a fertilized egg needs to implant. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T21#GNS312_U1_T21_h4)

question: How does Asherman syndrome primarily cause infertility in women?

options.A: Excessive production of hostile cervical mucus that destroys viable sperm cells
options.B: Mechanical torsion of the fallopian tubes caused by pelvic scar tissue
options.C: Formation of scar tissue inside the uterus that reduces the healthy lining
options.D: Premature depletion of ovarian follicles due to retrograde hormonal feedback

explanation: Asherman syndrome causes scar tissue to form inside the uterus, leaving too little healthy lining for an embryo to attach and grow. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T21#GNS312_U1_T21_h4)

question: How does cigarette smoking directly affect a woman's reproductive system?

options.A: It causes immediate and permanent closure of the cervix
options.B: It triggers rapid growth of benign submucosal fibroids
options.C: It speeds up the loss of eggs and causes early aging of the ovaries
options.D: It prevents the pituitary gland from producing prolactin

explanation: Chemicals in cigarette smoke damage ovarian tissue, leading to a faster loss of eggs and a shorter reproductive lifespan. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T21#GNS312_U1_T21_h5)

question: Why can being severely overweight or extremely underweight both cause trouble getting pregnant?

options.A: Both factors eliminate the production of luteinizing hormone entirely
options.B: Both states upset hormone balance and interrupt normal ovulation
options.C: Both conditions cause immediate anatomical blockage of the fallopian tubes
options.D: Both lifestyles trigger autoimmune destruction of the uterine lining

explanation: Extreme body weight affects how estrogen is stored and released, which can stop regular ovulation and lower the chances of conception. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T21#GNS312_U1_T21_h5)

question: What is the main reason a doctor orders a hysterosalpingogram during a fertility checkup?

options.A: To measure baseline serum progesterone levels after ovulation
options.B: To detect active chlamydia infections within the cervix
options.C: To count the exact number of resting ovarian follicles
options.D: To look at the shape of the uterus and see if the fallopian tubes are open

explanation: A hysterosalpingogram uses contrast dye and X-rays to create pictures of the inside of the uterus and check if the fallopian tubes are clear. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T21#GNS312_U1_T21_h6)

question: When is a blood test for progesterone usually done during a menstrual cycle to check if ovulation happened?

options.A: Day 14 regardless of overall cycle length
options.B: Day 21 of a standard twenty-eight-day menstrual cycle
options.D: Immediately at the onset of the luteinizing hormone surge

explanation: Progesterone levels peak about a week before a normal period begins, making day twenty-one the standard time to confirm ovulation in a twenty-eight-day cycle. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T21#GNS312_U1_T21_h6)

question: Which medication is commonly given first to help stimulate ovulation in women who are not releasing eggs?
explanation: Clomiphene citrate tricks the brain into releasing hormones that stimulate the ovaries to produce and release an egg. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T21#GNS312_U1_T21_h7)

question: What is the best nursing approach when caring for a patient who has just been diagnosed with physical causes of infertility?

options.A: Reassure the patient that natural conception will occur within one month
options.B: Focus entirely on surgical preparation without discussing emotional concerns
options.C: Offer a listening ear, clear information, and emotional support resources
options.D: Advise immediate discontinuation of all prescribed hormonal medications

explanation: Infertility causes a lot of emotional stress, so nurses need to combine practical health education with warm emotional support. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T21#GNS312_U1_T21_h7)
